evaluations.evidence: search and discover music using content identification or fingerprinting
evaluations.rationale: Scope is broad (search + discovery) and the capability could range from simple fingerprint lookup to full-scale identification pipeline and UX, making estimation difficult.

evaluations.evidence: search and discover music based on my profile
evaluations.rationale: Underspecified what 'profile' contains and what 'discover' entails (ranking, recommendations, filters), leading to wide implementation variance.

evaluations.evidence: search and discover music based on other users similar to myself
evaluations.rationale: Requires defining similarity model, data sources, and discovery UX; too many open choices for a reasonable estimate.

evaluations.evidence: search and discover music or ringback tones similar to a given music video based on content similarity
evaluations.rationale: Very broad: multiple media types and 'content similarity' could mean audio, visual, metadata, or combined approaches; hard to size.

evaluations.evidence: exploiting enriched metadata and image tags
evaluations.rationale: Does not specify which metadata/tags, how they are obtained, or what discovery features are included; scope can expand significantly.

evaluations.evidence: upload tagged videos and have tags available for all further processing steps
evaluations.rationale: Clear functional behavior (upload + persist tags for downstream use) that can be estimated without defining all downstream steps.

evaluations.evidence: view thumbnail sequences of video segments
evaluations.rationale: Concrete UI capability (display thumbnail sequences for segments) with bounded scope suitable for estimation.

evaluations.evidence: get info about similar video items and segments
evaluations.rationale: ‘Similar’ and ‘info’ are undefined (similarity method, returned fields, UI/API), creating large estimation uncertainty.

evaluations.evidence: get info about perceptually similar video items and segments
evaluations.rationale: Perceptual similarity can imply complex CV/AV models and indexing; outputs and constraints are unspecified, making it hard to estimate.

evaluations.evidence: receive content recommendations from similar profiles
evaluations.rationale: Recommendation logic, definition of profiles/similarity, and delivery mechanism are not specified; scope can vary widely.

evaluations.evidence: recommendations based on most relevant news events in my area
evaluations.rationale: Requires defining 'relevant news events', sourcing news, geolocation, and recommendation approach; too underspecified for estimation.

evaluations.evidence: identify persons in videos, and receive related information about them
evaluations.rationale: Person identification in video plus 'related information' is a large, complex, and open-ended requirement without boundaries.

evaluations.evidence: identify products in videos, and receive related information about them
evaluations.rationale: Product recognition in video and information retrieval are broad and unspecified (catalogs, accuracy, UI), preventing reliable estimation.

evaluations.evidence: identify broadcaster logos in videos, and receive related information about them
evaluations.rationale: Logo detection may be estimatable, but 'related information' and operational constraints are unspecified, expanding scope unpredictably.

evaluations.evidence: identify brands in videos, and receive related information about them
evaluations.rationale: Brand identification is broad (logos, products, text) and 'related information' is undefined; too open-ended to estimate.

evaluations.evidence: take a picture or upload an image, so that I am recommended with videos related to that picture or image
evaluations.rationale: Image-to-video recommendation requires defining 'related', matching approach, and UX; large solution space makes estimation difficult.

evaluations.evidence: walk around, access content using a geographical map and be informed if there are videos covering the area, monuments or any other relevant point of interest
evaluations.rationale: Combines multiple capabilities (map UI, geofencing, POI detection, notifications) and includes open-ended 'any other relevant point of interest'.

evaluations.evidence: search content items using automatic speech recognition
evaluations.rationale: ASR-based search could mean integrating an ASR service, building indexing, handling languages, and UI; insufficiently bounded for estimation.

evaluations.evidence: see, validate and edit segmentation of videos
evaluations.rationale: Admin workflow is clear (view/validate/edit segmentation); while non-trivial, it is sufficiently defined to estimate.

evaluations.evidence: annotate news video segments and extract a topic for each segment
evaluations.rationale: Bounded admin task (annotation + topic assignment per segment) that can be planned and estimated.

evaluations.evidence: filter and rank videos based on A/V quality aspects
evaluations.rationale: ‘A/V quality aspects’ are not defined (metrics, thresholds, models), so the effort can range from simple heuristics to complex analysis.

evaluations.evidence: quick assessment of whether audio material has been edited before the upload
evaluations.rationale: Detection of prior editing is a complex signal-processing/forensics problem with unclear approach and acceptance criteria, hard to estimate.

evaluations.evidence: prefilter nudity content
evaluations.rationale: Could range from simple keyword/tag filtering to ML-based image/video nudity detection; not bounded enough for estimation.

evaluations.evidence: prefilter content using search based on low­level asset information
evaluations.rationale: Low-level asset information and search capabilities are unspecified (fields, indexing, UI), making scope unclear.

evaluations.evidence: automatically validated the ingested contents for copyright infringement
evaluations.rationale: Copyright infringement detection/validation is broad and legally/technically complex with undefined method and boundaries.

evaluations.evidence: prefilter the content using search on high­level asset information such as metadata and tags
evaluations.rationale: Search/prefilter behavior and supported metadata/tags are not specified; could be minimal filtering or full search platform.

evaluations.evidence: assess how interesting or appealing or complex a picture is based on automated analysis, citizen annotations, and comments on Talk
evaluations.rationale: Subjective constructs (interesting/appealing/complex) and multi-source analysis are not operationalized, making estimation unreliable.

evaluations.evidence: detect when a scientist should be prompted to look at a subject, based on annotations and information from Talk comments
evaluations.rationale: Trigger conditions and detection logic are unspecified and potentially complex (NLP + rules/ML), so scope is hard to estimate.

evaluations.evidence: identify volunteer types
evaluations.rationale: ‘Volunteer types’ is undefined (taxonomy, features, method), ranging from simple segmentation to complex modeling.

evaluations.evidence: preclassify the Galaxy Zoo images using simple low­level image features
evaluations.rationale: Bounded by 'simple low-level image features' and a specific dataset context, enabling reasonable estimation.

evaluations.evidence: automatically detect Snapshot Serengeti images with no classifiable animals in them
evaluations.rationale: Specific detection task with clear outcome (empty/no classifiable animals) that can be estimated.

evaluations.evidence: automatic image series detection for the case of timestamping malfunction
evaluations.rationale: ‘Image series detection’ and handling of timestamp malfunction are not defined (rules, inputs, outputs), leaving broad solution space.

evaluations.evidence: automatic animal species preclassification in Snapshot Serengeti
evaluations.rationale: Species preclassification can vary from coarse grouping to full multi-class ML with training/validation; not bounded enough to estimate.

evaluations.evidence: automatic animal attribute preclassification in Snapshot Serengeti
evaluations.rationale: Attributes are unspecified (e.g., behavior, age, sex), which strongly affects complexity and estimation.

evaluations.evidence: automatic animal number detection in Snapshot Serengeti
evaluations.rationale: Counting animals can range from simple heuristics to complex detection in clutter/occlusion; constraints and accuracy targets are missing.

evaluations.evidence: automatic segmentation or localization of plankton in Plankton Portal
evaluations.rationale: ‘Segmentation or localization’ indicates alternative scopes and methods; without specifying which, estimation is difficult.

evaluations.evidence: automatically detect Plankton Portal images with no classifiable plankton in them
evaluations.rationale: Clear binary detection objective (no classifiable plankton) with bounded scope suitable for estimation.

evaluations.evidence: automatic detection of plankton size or orientation
evaluations.rationale: Uses 'or' (two different tasks) and lacks definition of measurement method/precision, making effort hard to estimate.

evaluations.evidence: automatic preclassification of plankton species
evaluations.rationale: Species set, granularity, and performance expectations are unspecified; could be small or very large ML effort.

evaluations.evidence: perform automatic worm motion analysis to reduce video duration
evaluations.rationale: Motion analysis approach and what 'reduce video duration' means (summarization rules, thresholds) are unclear, affecting scope.

evaluations.evidence: detect the time ... where the worm lays an egg
evaluations.rationale: Event detection in video is complex and acceptance criteria (precision/recall, annotation needs) are not specified, making estimation hard.

evaluations.evidence: detect important features such as areas of flooding, damage, temporary shelters, blocked roads etc in the satellite images
evaluations.rationale: Multiple feature types with 'etc' implies open-ended scope; each feature class changes complexity substantially.

evaluations.evidence: assess the probability/weight of a volunteer’s classification based on their experience
evaluations.rationale: Weighting model, definition of experience, and how weights are used are unspecified; could be simple rules or complex modeling.

evaluations.evidence: prefiltering of the images to remove artefacts such as bright stars and camera read errors
evaluations.rationale: Artefact types and removal approach are not bounded; could involve multiple detection/correction pipelines with varying complexity.

evaluations.evidence: detect moving and transient objects in the images
evaluations.rationale: ‘Moving and transient objects’ is broad and depends on data modality/time series assumptions not stated, making estimation uncertain.

evaluations.evidence: remove background noise and distracting sounds from the audio files
evaluations.rationale: Audio enhancement scope is broad (noise vs distracting sounds) and quality targets are unspecified, leading to wide effort range.

evaluations.evidence: group whale calls that are similar
evaluations.rationale: Similarity definition, grouping method (clustering, labeling), and outputs are unspecified; could be simple or complex ML pipeline.

evaluations.evidence: identify the number of whales heard in a single audio file
evaluations.rationale: Counting individuals from audio is complex and depends on assumptions and accuracy requirements not provided, hindering estimation.

evaluations.evidence: know when I should interrupt a volunteer
evaluations.rationale: ‘When to interrupt’ lacks triggers, channels, and decision logic; could entail extensive behavioral modeling and experimentation.

evaluations.evidence: know whether I should interrupt a volunteer with text, an image, or a video
evaluations.rationale: Requires defining interruption strategy and selection logic among modalities; underspecified and potentially large scope.

evaluations.evidence: know when I should educate a volunteer
evaluations.rationale: Education triggers and decision criteria are not defined; could range from simple rules to complex personalization.

evaluations.evidence: know whether I should educate a volunteer with text, an image, or a video
evaluations.rationale: Modality selection for education is underspecified and could require content strategy, experimentation, and personalization logic.

evaluations.evidence: know which piece of education I should give to a volunteer
evaluations.rationale: Does not define the education content set, selection criteria, or delivery context; scope is open-ended and hard to estimate.

evaluations.evidence: know when a volunteer has made an interesting comment on a subject
evaluations.rationale: ‘Interesting comment’ is subjective and not operationalized; could require NLP models and tuning, making estimation difficult.

evaluations.evidence: know when Zoonibot should comment on a subject
evaluations.rationale: Triggering logic for bot comments is unspecified and potentially complex (context, policies), preventing reliable estimation.

evaluations.evidence: know when Zoonibot should give an explanation
evaluations.rationale: No definition of explanation types, triggers, or constraints; scope can expand widely, making estimation hard.

evaluations.evidence: know what Zoonibot should say to a volunteer
evaluations.rationale: Open-ended natural language generation/content authoring problem without boundaries or scenarios; not estimatable as a single story.

evaluations.evidence: group subjects by similarity
evaluations.rationale: Similarity basis, subject type, grouping outputs, and scale are unspecified; could range from simple metadata grouping to complex ML.

evaluations.evidence: recommend different projects to volunteers based on their previous experiences
evaluations.rationale: Recommendation approach, definition of experiences, and delivery UX are not specified; broad scope makes estimation difficult.

evaluations.evidence: see a summary of articles, so that I reuse them
evaluations.rationale: ‘Summary of articles’ is underspecified (which articles, summary type/length, where shown), leading to multiple plausible implementations.
